newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMAN POLITICIANS STEP INTO DUNDEE ROW. [CORRECTED 16:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMAN POLITICIANS STEP INTO DUNDEE ROW. [CORRECTED 16:30 GMT]

text.p: Politicians have stepped into the row over whether Karlsruhe's South African striker Sean Dundee should be granted German citizenship.
Dundee, the Bundesliga's leading scorer who hopes to play for Germany, is using a fast-track method reserved for cases of "public interest" in his bid to be naturalised.

Cem Ozdemir, of the opposition Greens party, complained in Friday's Rhein-Neckar Zeitung newspaper: "Every time Dundee scores, we read he is closer to citizenship. The same law should apply for everyone."

Klaus Riegert, sports policy spokesman for Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (Corrects spelling and role of Riegert) backed the rule allowing sports people to jump the queue. "If a sports star wins a medal, the whole country is pleased," he said.
Dundee's decision also provoked anger in his native country, where some politicians have accused him of turning his back on South Africa.

The German Soccer Federation backs Dundee's claim but insists it has not put any pressure on the Interior Ministry to approve the application so the player can make his debut against Northern Ireland in a World Cup qualifier next month.
National coach Berti Vogts is apparently keen for Dundee to be available for the match in Nuremberg.
The 23-year-old Dundee, also courted by the Republic of Ireland earlier this year, is following a path well-trodden by foreign sports stars who have adopted German citizenship.
High jumper Alina Astafei and promising tennis star Alex Radulescu have both rejected their native Romania to become Germans in recent years.
Dundee began his Bundesliga career last season as an amateur with Karlsruhe, but forced his way into the first team and scored 16 league goals. He has nine so far this season.
